if:
Begins a conditional statement. Runs its block when `condition` is truthy (anything except `nil` or `false`).

```luau
if condition then ... end
```
elseif:
Chains another condition onto an `if`, checked only if all preceding conditions were false.

```luau
if condition then ... elseif other then ... end
```
then:
Separates an `if`/`elseif` condition from the block that runs when it's true.

```luau
if condition then ... end
```
else:
Runs its block when none of the preceding `if`/`elseif` conditions were true.

```luau
if condition then ... else ... end
```
while:
Repeats its block for as long as `condition` remains truthy, checked before each iteration.

```luau
while condition do ... end
```
do: Introduces the body of a loop or a standalone `do ... end` scoping block.
repeat:
Repeats its block at least once, checking the condition after each iteration (unlike `while`, which checks first).

```luau
repeat ... until condition
```
until:
Ends a `repeat` loop's body and gives the condition that stops it. Locals declared in the loop body are visible in this condition.

```luau
repeat ... until condition
```
for:
Repeats its block, either counting through a numeric range or iterating over a table/iterator.

```luau
for i = start, stop, step do ... end
for k, v in iterable do ... end
```
in:
Separates the loop variables from the value being iterated in a generic `for` loop.

```luau
for k, v in iterable do ... end
```
return: Exits the current function immediately, optionally producing one or more values back to the caller.
break: Exits the innermost enclosing loop (`while`, `repeat`, or `for`) immediately.
continue: Skips the rest of the current loop iteration and jumps to the next one.
function:
Defines a function.

```luau
function name(...) ... end
local function name(...) ... end
```
local:
Declares a new variable (or function) scoped to the current block, shadowing any outer variable of the same name.

```luau
local x = value
local function f() ... end
```
const:
Declares a local identical to `local`, except it's a syntax error to reassign it after initialization.

```luau
const x = value
```
const_function:
Declares a function whose name can't be reassigned -- combines `local function`'s scoping with `const`'s reassignment restriction.

```luau
const function f() ... end
```
class_const:
Marks a class field as immutable once the object is constructed -- unlike a local `const`, this is about the field, not a variable binding.

```luau
class Name
    private const field: type
end
```
type:
Declares a type alias, giving a name to a type for reuse elsewhere.

```luau
type Name = ...
```
export_type:
Declares a type alias and makes it available to other files that require this module -- combines `type` with `export`'s visibility across module boundaries.

```luau
export type Name = ...
```
declare:
Declares an ambient global, function, or extern type with no implementation -- used in definition files to describe types provided by the host environment.

```luau
declare function f(...): ...
declare class Name ... end
```
class:
Defines a class: a constructor, fields, and methods, with `public`/`private` visibility. Constructing an instance calls the class value like a function.

```luau
class Name(...) ... end
```
export_class:
Defines a class and makes it available to other files that require this module -- combines `class` with `export`'s visibility across module boundaries.

```luau
export class Name(...) ... end
```
extends:
Declares that an extern type inherits the members of a parent extern type.

```luau
declare class Child extends Parent ... end
```
public:
Marks a class field or method as part of the class's external API, visible outside the class body.

```luau
class Name
    public field: type
end
```
private:
Marks a class field or method as internal-only, accessible only from within the class's own methods.

```luau
class Name
    private field: type
end
```
nil: The absence of a value. `nil` is falsy, and any unassigned variable or missing table key evaluates to it.
false: The boolean value representing falsehood. Along with `nil`, this is one of only two falsy values in Luau.
